# Strategy Succession engineering candidate

Plan a software release, adapt that project's requirements, then repair its
actual preceding plan while preserving committed work. One explicit approval
starts the three bounded phases. Inspect the selected method, independently
checked schedule, retained strategy records, actual ledger and rejected or
deferred improvements.

This additive candidate uses the public **AGI ALPHA 1.42.0** runtime's signed
journal, action gateway and authenticated local request boundary. It includes the
fixed browser interface, worker, exact scientific source subset, source guards,
licenses and an operator profile. It installs no background service and creates
no credential. Launch requires an **existing approved operator home**.

The candidate version is **0.1.0rc1**. It is intended for the existing Alpha
repository's reviewed `contrib/strategy_succession` lane and a later additive
asset through the existing publisher. A built wheel is not a public software
release or production admission.

## Install and open

Use the independently verified public runtime wheel and this candidate's actual
wheel in a **separate Python 3.12 virtual environment**. Preserve every existing
Alpha installation; do not downgrade a newer accepted runtime. The public runtime download is:

[alpha_factory_v1-1.42.0-py3-none-any.whl](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGI-Alpha-Agent-v0/releases/download/v1.42.0/alpha_factory_v1-1.42.0-py3-none-any.whl)

Its SHA-256 is
`fff8c6c8a8dbeeebf1f91cc8e9a3fae17113baac93b6ed0d6096ecb59d072554`.
The installation profile also checks the installed Alpha Python source. Do not
assume a PyPI distribution provides these exact public bytes.

```sh
python3.12 -m venv /absolute/path/to/strategy-candidate-env
. /absolute/path/to/strategy-candidate-env/bin/activate
python -m pip install ./alpha_factory_v1-1.42.0-py3-none-any.whl
python -m pip install ./agi_alpha_strategy_succession_engineering-0.1.0rc1-py3-none-any.whl
strategy-succession-engineering --home /absolute/path/to/existing-approved-operator-home
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8768`. Enter the existing operator token in the local page;
it stays only in tab memory. Choose **Start**, inspect the fixed input, source,
expiry and separate budgets, then **Approve and start work**. Review the actual
results and use **Keep** or **Export**. **Pause** and **Stop** fence the executor
at its next bounded checkpoint. See [the operator guide](docs/operator.md) before
handling interrupted or uncertain work.

The ordinary fixed portfolio is available without native solver permission.
The separately admitted native specialist requires an explicit operator launch:

```sh
strategy-succession-engineering --home /absolute/path/to/existing-approved-operator-home --native
```

`--native` remains local planning work. It does not enable a desktop, network
agent, live contract route or physical operation. Each attempted native call
charges its fixed solve **allowance** before execution; observed solver, process
wall and CPU measurements remain separate.

## Qualified scope

| Component | Current engineering acceptance scope |
| --- | --- |
| Host | Linux x86_64, CPython 3.12.14 |
| Runtime | Actual public Alpha wheel 1.42.0 and exact source identities in the installation profile |
| Worker | Node.js 24.22.1; fixed operator-installed methods |
| Native specialist | SciPy 1.17.0; separate explicit local allowance |
| Inputs | Public or synthetic nonpersonal `release-plan/v1` planning data within the fixed grammar |
| Work | Initial plan → changed requirements → repair derived from the actual checked preceding result |
| Improvement | Bounded strategy construction and fresh engineering checks; correctness and economic admission remain separate |
| Authority | Local approved finite request only; exported proof and authority remain empty |

Other operating systems, Python/Node versions, runtime source identities and
product combinations remain unqualified. The launcher refuses an unknown Alpha
runtime version or changed guarded source. This candidate does not qualify the
held native Harness/bridge, Fleet, a four-product installation, general desktop
work or the requested public-repository maintenance mission.

`worker/SCIENTIFIC_PROVENANCE.json` and `worker/SOURCE_FILES.json` preserve the
exact source subset from scientific freeze
`7e5a1dd2dcf7eb00ec055f1858d5dd722cc950f15f33314bb94c456c753845a7`.
The engineering worker, native repair kernel, transport and UI are separate
additions. Their development tests and examples do not replace or rerun the
frozen study's primary results. A retained strategy can be correctness-qualified
while economic admission remains on hold. Human effort, hardware cost, monetary
cost, commercial value, acceleration and revenue remain unknown unless
separately measured.

## Build and verify the package

The package includes only explicitly listed payloads. Builds fail if the current
worker or installation profile disagrees with source; the build does not rewrite
approval hashes. Private homes, credentials, local environments, caches and
development receipts are excluded.

```sh
python -m pip install setuptools==84.1.0 wheel==0.48.0
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1792800000 python -m pip wheel --no-build-isolation --no-deps . --wheel-dir /absolute/path/to/build-one
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1792800000 python -m pip wheel --no-build-isolation --no-deps . --wheel-dir /absolute/path/to/build-two
```

Compare the two wheel SHA-256 hashes, then install the actual wheel into a
different environment outside the source checkout. Verify every guarded package
file, `--help`, the installation profile and the authenticated local API journey.
`requirements-qualification.txt` pins the complete observed core dependency
closure; it is a version inventory, not a claim that dependency wheel hashes or
every platform have been qualified. The package and public runtime wheel have
their own exact byte identities. Browser acceptance remains a separate check.

__version__ = "0.1.0rc1"

# Operate the fixed Strategy Succession candidate

Use an existing approved Alpha operator home. This program never initializes an
operator, grants a new key, changes security settings, funds work or installs a
daemon. The runtime profile admits only exact public Alpha 1.42.0 source and the
listed fixed worker/transport/UI bytes. A different version or source identity
is unqualified and must receive separate review; changing a label or rebuilding
does not admit it.

## Start useful work

1. Create and activate a separate Python 3.12 virtual environment, then install
   the verified public Alpha wheel and this candidate wheel there. Preserve all
   existing accepted Alpha environments. Check the package/profile identities.
2. Launch `strategy-succession-engineering --home /absolute/path/to/existing-approved-home`.
   The server binds only `127.0.0.1`, uses the existing token and disables access
   logging. Add `--native` only within an explicitly approved local solver scope.
3. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8768`. Enter the existing operator token using your
   approved credential-access method. The page clears the input after connection
   and keeps the token in memory only. Do not place it in URLs, exports, prompts
   or browser storage.
4. Choose **Start**. The server prepares a fixed plan; preparation performs no
   mission work. Inspect its exact input, executor identity, source hash,
   separate service/improvement caps and expiry. Editing the form does not
   change that prepared plan: choose Start again for different inputs.
5. Approve that exact plan and start it. One bounded worker action executes the
   initial plan, changed requirements and repair. The browser does not trigger
   the phases one by one. Inspect each checked schedule and the method that
   actually supplied it. Keep or export useful results and strategy records.

The supported planning grammar contains 1–18 jobs, bounded durations/crew,
dependencies and a finite calendar. It accepts public or synthetic nonpersonal
data. It produces planning artifacts. It does not inspect arbitrary repositories,
execute imported code, control a general desktop or cause physical work.

The ordinary portfolio remains a valid incumbent. Native deadline/makespan
specialists and the matching repair specialist are available only when the
operator enables their separate allowance. Construction may defer, reject a
candidate or retain the incumbent. Local correctness qualification does not
establish economic value or production authority.

## Budgets and evidence

Service work and improvement work have separate protected accounts. A journey
reserves both caps atomically before the fixed action gateway dispatches it. The
browser cannot select a host path, executable, endpoint, policy, source or cap.
The process admits one active request; request count, lease and expiry are
bounded by the installed profile.

`service_work` and `improvement_work` are declared work units.
`native_calls` counts actual attempted calls. The legacy API field
`native_solve_seconds` records **charged solve allowance seconds**: two seconds
are charged before each fixed two-second native attempt, including failed or
uncertain attempts. It is not measured CPU or elapsed time. The actual solver's
reported timing, wrapper/process wall time, CPU, import/check time and unknown
opaque work remain separate telemetry. Never convert one counter into another
or turn these figures into monetary savings. Human effort, device cost and
monetary cost remain unknown.

The signed Alpha journal records reservations, observed increments, source and
request commitments. Each actually checked phase receipt is committed before
the worker is acknowledged and allowed to proceed. It includes the task,
selected method, result, independent checker output and original receipt hash;
the transport adds source/plan binding and a separate digest. At most three
ordered partial receipts are admitted. Duplicates cannot add another artifact,
repeat cost increments or relabel a prior delivery as another phase.

Known completion commits the result and actual separate counters before the
HTTP reply. A known verification failure is retained as rejected with its costs.
Exported records carry local attribution and empty proof/authority lists.
Self-reported confidence, a signature or a native solver status alone is not
independent correctness proof. Scientific results, engineering checks,
operational permission and production admission remain distinct.

## Pause and Stop

**Pause** fences new work and interrupts active work at its next bounded
checkpoint. **Stop** permanently revokes this installed envelope. The existing
Alpha journal-wide pause also fences preparation, approval, reservation,
checkpoints and completion. Native or other fixed child processes are bounded
and killed on refusal; an in-flight operation can have an uncertain outcome.

Closing or disconnecting the browser does not terminate an already running
local executor. Its one explicitly approved bounded request may continue until
completion, STOP, lease expiry or process failure. The browser is not an
unattended agent. Stopping the local process stops further progress; this
candidate installs no background service or indefinite recurrence.

A retained `running` record is not proof that its process is still active.
Status distinguishes work observed in this executor from **awaiting evidence**,
and separately reports whether the recorded lease is current or expired. A
restarted executor does not guess that the old process completed, disappeared
or is safe to replay.

## Recover an UNKNOWN outcome

Do not interpret a lost response, stale running lease, partial result, process
crash or timeout as safe failure. The full uncertain request reservation remains
charged. Already committed phase receipts survive. They do not authorize the
remaining phases to resume.

1. Reconnect and inspect retained status, the active/expired lease, observed
   counters, partial receipts and export. A completed duplicate returns the
   original committed outcome without executing again.
2. Verify the executor process and any child have stopped. A current active
   lease cannot be reconciled. Inspect the actual target/result; do not infer
   that unobserved work was free or never ran.
3. For an unknown or stale expired running record, use the existing
   `/api/strategy-executor/reconcile` operation with `plan_id`, the exact current
   status `record_digest` and an operator `note` describing what was observed.
   This records a judgment; it grants no proof and refunds no unknown allowance.
4. The reconciled plan remains permanently non-replayable. Further work needs a
   fresh plan and explicit approval within remaining protected capacity. A
   stopped envelope cannot be resumed. Obtain a separately reviewed installation
   or policy decision when capacity or authority is unavailable.

Do not replay phase commands manually to bypass this refusal. No automatic
prompt-by-prompt recovery, duplicate delivery retry, grant restoration or
production promotion is implemented.

## Restore and rollback

Use the existing Alpha verified backup procedure for private operator recovery;
keep private backups separate from mission exports. A copied or restored journal
at another home does not inherit this transport's old execution grants: approval
binds the original local home/database incarnation, and the transport refuses a
different incarnation. Historical signed evidence remains inspectable. Fresh
local execution requires an explicit separately reviewed authorization path;
do not clear or rewrite the old signed records.

Keep the last accepted public Alpha release and candidate package intact.
Rollback means stop this candidate, inspect and reconcile uncertain work, then
use the previously accepted installation through its own authorized process.
It does not mean downgrading source under an old live grant, rewriting pins or
erasing rejected/failing histories. This engineering contribution does not clear
any held Harness/bridge or Fleet review, merge or native execution restriction.

## Read the cost record

Construction and service use different protected accounts. The ledger records failed proposals, current checks, retrieval, retained reports and workbench integration. Native calls reserve two solve seconds before each attempt; physical solver/startup/checker wall and CPU measurements stay separate. These allowances are not measured CPU time or money.

The report keeps API acceptance, browser acceptance and crash/recovery attempts separate. A killed request retains its full unknown reservation, even when one checked phase survives. It is not a free failed attempt. No automatic retry is available.

Model inference calls are zero for these fixed algorithms; model-assisted authorship, setup and review effort remain unknown. Python HTTP/journal/cryptographic overhead, whole QA/development cost, hardware and currency totals are not fully measured. Forecast maintenance is a declared assumption, not an incurred saving. No synthetic work-unit reduction is revenue or profit.

"""Build only the reviewed source and exact declared runtime payload."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import re
import tomllib

from setuptools import setup
from setuptools.command.build_py import build_py

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def guarded_sources() -> None:
    """Refuse a stale manifest instead of regenerating source approval."""
    profile = json.loads((ROOT / "ENGINEERING_MANIFEST.json").read_text())
    if profile.get("schema") != "strategy-engineering-installation/v1":
        raise ValueError("Expected the reviewed engineering installation profile")
    project = tomllib.loads((ROOT / "pyproject.toml").read_text())
    payload = set(project["tool"]["setuptools"]["package-data"]["strategy_succession_engineering"])
    payload.update({"serve.py", "__init__.py"})
    files = profile["files"]
    if not isinstance(files, dict) or not 1 <= len(files) <= 256:
        raise ValueError("Invalid exact installed file inventory")
    if set(files) != payload - {"ENGINEERING_MANIFEST.json"}:
        raise ValueError("Installation profile must hash the exact complete package payload")
    for name, expected in files.items():
        relative = PurePosixPath(name)
        if (
            relative.is_absolute()
            or relative.as_posix() != name
            or any(p in {"", ".", ".."} for p in name.split("/"))
            or "\\" in name
            or name not in payload
        ):
            raise ValueError("Installation profile requests an unlisted package file")
        path = ROOT / name
        if not isinstance(expected, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", expected):
            raise ValueError("Installation profile has an invalid source hash")
        if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file() or hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != expected:
            raise ValueError(
                "Source differs from the reviewed installation manifest; do not regenerate it during build"
            )
    worker = json.loads((ROOT / "worker" / "SOURCE_FILES.json").read_text())
    if worker.get("scientific_source_hash") != profile["scientific_source_hash"]:
        raise ValueError("Scientific source identity is inconsistent")
    for entry in worker["files"]:
        name = "worker/" + entry["path"]
        if files.get(name) != entry["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Worker source inventory is not covered by the reviewed package profile")


class GuardedBuild(build_py):
    def find_package_modules(self, package: str, package_dir: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
        modules = super().find_package_modules(package, package_dir)
        if any(module not in {"__init__", "serve", "setup"} for _, module, _ in modules):
            raise ValueError("Unexpected Python module at the fixed package root")
        return [entry for entry in modules if entry[1] in {"__init__", "serve"}]

    def run(self) -> None:
        guarded_sources()
        super().run()


setup(cmdclass={"build_py": GuardedBuild})

# Fixed Strategy executor transport

This is an additive engineering contribution for the existing Strategy Succession
owner. It does not change the frozen experiment, original Harness, Fleet,
publication ownership or production authority. It is not repository maintenance
or a general desktop executor.

`strategy_executor.py` reuses the actual Alpha runtime `Journal`, `ActionGateway`
and `RequestBoundary`. Its narrow application exposes only the fixed strategy
routes and optional three operator-installed static assets. It does not weaken
CORS or expose the unrelated runtime operations.

## Operator interface

Import `SourceFile`, `Limits`, `ExecutorPolicy`, `create_strategy_app`. Supply the
existing configured `Journal`, the reviewed fixed worker instance, and a policy.
Do not initialize another journal automatically or create a credential in this
transport. `create_strategy_app` reads the existing journal's `api.token`.

`SourceFile(label, path, sha256)` lists every operator-installed worker/scientific
source whose identity is part of approval. Paths stay local. The public envelope
shows only their combined hash. Missing, linked, changed or oversized files fail
closed. These checks do not sandbox code or establish review eligibility.

`Limits(service_work, improvement_work, native_calls, native_solve_seconds)` has
separate service and construction accounts. `ExecutorPolicy` maps the installed
methods to per-plan limits and specifies aggregate limits, maximum request count,
approval lifetime, request lease and `allow_native` (false by default). The
browser cannot provide these settings. A changed policy is refused against an
existing transport journal record; a legitimate reviewed change needs its own
explicit operator migration/installation decision.

Approval also binds the existing home/database filesystem incarnation through a
nonsecret digest. A copied/restored journal in another home does not inherit
execution approval. The private backup still verifies as historical evidence;
the transport refuses to operate its inherited grants. This creates no new key
or persistent credential.

Supported method names are `run-mission`, `construct` and `run-journey`.
`run-mission` cannot spend construction units; `construct` cannot spend service
units. `run-journey` reserves both accounts in one transaction. It may execute its
fixed successive phases after one approval without additional browser prompts.

The worker implements:

```python
execute(method, payload, limits, checkpoint) -> {
    "result": {...},
    "costs": {"service_work": 0, "improvement_work": 0, "native_calls": 0,
              "native_solve_seconds": 0.0, "unknown_costs": ["human effort"]},
    "source_hash": limits["source_hash"], "verified": True
}
```

Worker-facing limits also contain `wall_seconds`, `allow_native` and
`source_hash`. The source hash covers the operator-listed implementation files;
the original scientific freeze identity should be reported separately inside the
result. The worker must validate its exact fixed input schema. Browser input is
data; it cannot select a command, module, host path, executable or endpoint.

Call `checkpoint()` before every bounded phase. Call
`checkpoint(native_calls=1, native_solve_seconds=2)` before each fixed two-second native attempt and pass exact known work
increments as they become available. Each increment is retained before the next
operation. Final cumulative counters must cover these increments and remain
within the approved caps. The legacy field `native_solve_seconds` means charged
solve allowance seconds, including failed or uncertain attempts. Actual observed
solver time, process CPU and wrapper wall time remain separately labelled
telemetry. Work units are not money, CPU or revenue.

After an actually checked phase, the fixed worker may call
`checkpoint(receipt=partial, **increments)` before proceeding. The optional
partial has exactly `phase_index` (0–2), `receipt_hash`, `task`, `result`,
`checker`, and `selectedmethod`. Its original receipt hash binds the fixed
scientific source and current executor source, with empty proof/authority lists.
The transport checks its integer-only canonical bytes and adds a separate digest
binding the current plan and local policy. At most three ordered receipts fit
within the installed output-byte cap, and they commit to the signed journal
before the callback acknowledges them. They survive STOP, exceptions, restart,
reconciliation and export even when the overall request remains unknown.

An exact duplicate partial does not append another artifact. It must not repeat
cost increments; that combination is refused atomically. Different contents at
an existing phase index, out-of-order phases and relabelling an existing
receipt/task identity as a new phase are refused. Each new increment
is recorded once; the wrapper must not automatically resend acknowledged
increments. Partial results never grant automatic continuation or authority.

The callback must itself impose finite process/time bounds and terminate its
child process on checkpoint failure. The transport cannot forcibly preempt an
arbitrary in-process Python callback. Only reviewed fixed code is permitted;
there is no generated-code, host-shell or imported-code execution API.

## Browser protocol

Every API call uses `Authorization: Bearer ...` with the existing operator token.
Keep it only in browser memory, clear the credential input after connection, and
never put it in URLs, HTML, browser storage, logs or exports. Mutation requests
must be same-origin and have unambiguous bounded Content-Length framing.

| Request | JSON fields | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET `/api/strategy-executor/status` | none | State, exact plans, observed usage, aggregate reserved/spent/total, source availability, identity, record digest |
| POST `/api/strategy-executor/prepare` | `method`, `input`, `request_id` | Exact plan with `plan_id`, `plan_digest`, caps, source, identity, expiry |
| POST `/api/strategy-executor/approve` | `plan_id`, `plan_digest` | Exact locally approved plan |
| POST `/api/strategy-executor/run` | `plan_id`, `plan_digest` | Synchronous committed plan and outcome; poll status concurrently |
| POST `/api/strategy-executor/control` | `state`: `ready`, `paused` or `stopped` | Current state |
| POST `/api/strategy-executor/reconcile` | `plan_id`, current status `record_digest`, `note` | Inspected uncertain plan, permanently non-replayable |
| GET `/api/strategy-executor/export/{plan_id}` | none | Signed portable evidence; no credential or active grant |

The UI should describe local execution, disconnected/paused/stopped states,
approval expiry and unknown outcomes plainly. `completed` means the fixed worker
verification passed and the result was committed. A known verification failure is
retained as `rejected`, with its measured costs and no replay. Local attribution is
not independent verification or production admission.

## Stop, recovery and costs

Only one request executes per process/journal. Journal transactions also refuse
a second active request across service instances. A plan reserves its complete
caps before action dispatch. Completion commits the outcome hash and actual
separate counters before acknowledging the HTTP response. Duplicate delivery of
the same completed input returns that committed result, without executing again.
Reusing an idempotency identity for changed inputs is refused.
The existing journal-wide pause is checked at preparation, approval, reservation,
every worker checkpoint and completion, in addition to the strategy-specific
controls.

An exception, STOP, expired lease or lost process before commit leaves an unknown
outcome with its full cap reservations retained. A stale `running` record is not
treated as a safe failure. Inspect status/evidence, then reconcile using the
exact current record digest and an operator note. Reconciliation does not refund
unknown work or reopen the plan. New work requires a fresh plan and explicit
approval within remaining protected capacity. STOP is permanent for this
installed envelope. Pause fences active work at its next bounded checkpoint;
resume does not replay that interrupted request.

Closing the browser does not stop an already running local process. That process
may finish its explicitly approved finite request. Closing/stopping the local
executor process prevents further progress; no unattended service or scheduler
is installed by this contribution.

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/path/to/alpha:/path/to/transport python -m pytest -q -c /dev/null /path/to/transport/test_strategy_executor.py
```

confirmation inputs, results or acceptance criteria.
